title: Incommensurate spin fluctuations in one-dimensional Kondo metal CeCo2Ga8
authors: Yixuan Huang, P. Murgatroyd, Yi Wu, M. Cook, P. F. S. Rosa, E. D. Bauer, Asish K. Kundu, A. Rajapitamahuni, E. Vescovo, S. Zhang, V. Anil, P. Piyawongwatthana, N. Murai, M. Kofu, K. M. Shen, F. Ronning, Jian-Xin Zhu, A. Scheie
abstract: We present an experimental and numerical study of the spin fluctuations in 1D Kondo metal CeCo$_2$Ga$_8$. Using inelastic neutron spectroscopy, we measure highly one-dimensional magnetism with low-energy incommensurate short-ranged magnetic fluctuations. ARPES similarly shows a highly one-dimensional electronic band structure, confirming the one-dimensional nature of the system. We use density matrix renormalization group (DMRG) simulations of the 1D Kondo lattice model to interpret the measured spectrum, which successfully reproduce the neutron scattering features. We are thus able to place CeCo$_2$Ga$_8$ within the emergent incommensurate phase of the 1D Kondo lattice phase diagram, and demonstrate that the Kondo lattice simulated non-perturbatively is an accurate microscopic model for heavy fermion physics. This shows CeCo$_2$Ga$_8$ to be one-dimensional despite its complexities, and reveals a coexistence of low-energy Kondo and magnetic features in its inelastic spectrum.
summary: This work experimentally and numerically investigates the spin fluctuations in the 1D Kondo metal CeCo2Ga8. By combining inelastic neutron scattering and ARPES with DMRG simulations, the authors confirm the material's quasi-1D nature and place it within the incommensurate phase of the 1D Kondo lattice diagram. This validates the use of the Kondo lattice model as a microscopic description for heavy fermion behavior.
main_problem: The study aims to characterize the spin fluctuations and electronic structure in the 1D Kondo metal CeCo2Ga8 and determine if its behavior can be accurately modeled by the 1D Kondo lattice model.
main_result: The material exhibits highly one-dimensional electronic and magnetic behavior, showing incommensurate spin fluctuations that are successfully reproduced by non-perturbative DMRG simulations of the 1D Kondo lattice model.
method: The research combines experimental measurements using inelastic neutron spectroscopy and ARPES with theoretical interpretation via Density Matrix Renormalization Group (DMRG) simulations.
model_or_system: The physical system is the heavy fermion metal CeCo2Ga8, which is modeled using the 1D Kondo lattice model. This model describes the competition between Kondo screening and magnetic interactions.
key_observables: Incommensurate magnetic fluctuations ($\ell=0.354(2)$), quasi-1D electronic band structure (ARPES), and the localized spin susceptibility ($\chi_{SS}$).
important_parameters: Low-energy scale ($\approx 1 	ext{ meV}$), Kondo coupling strengths ($J_H, J_k$), and the dimensionality (highly 1D).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the Kondo lattice model is the appropriate minimal description for the heavy fermion physics, despite potential neglect of higher-dimensional bands.
figures_summary: Figures show neutron scattering intensity mapping out incommensurate peaks, ARPES contours confirming 1D dispersion, and DMRG results illustrating the spectral evolution across different theoretical phases.
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by first presenting experimental evidence (neutron scattering and ARPES) confirming 1D, incommensurate fluctuations, followed by theoretical modeling using DMRG to map these features onto the known phase diagram of the 1D Kondo lattice.
why_interesting: The successful mapping of complex heavy fermion physics onto a solvable 1D quantum model (Kondo lattice) provides a powerful benchmark for understanding emergent quantum phases in strongly correlated materials.
